Nxeon hosting platform, Next.js/TS/React. Production is /opt/nxeon — do not touch directly, work in a worktree. There is existing WIP hero work at /opt/nxeon-wt-sghero (branch feature/singapore-hero-v5) — the owner just rejected that whole hero direction as "terrible" and wants to restart with ONE narrow, isolated piece: just the network-map graphic, built and perfected on its own before anything else touches the hero again. Work in a NEW worktree, don't touch the rejected hero files.

Read the reference image yourself before writing any code: /opt/nxeon/board-uploads/board/cmtacetu5000ghlgv9lr97mwy/c7778eb3a24b33135c5ddb53.png — full resolution, this is the literal design target, not inspiration. The owner's own words: "Treat the image as a design specification, not inspiration. The final component should visually reproduce the reference as closely as possible." And: "Do not move on to the rest of the page until this component is visually close to the reference. If the first implementation does not look close enough, iterate."

SCOPE — build ONLY this, nothing else:
A reusable component `SingaporeNetworkMap` (component only — no hero text, no nav, no pricing, no footer, no server card). It represents Nxeon's Singapore datacenter as a central hub connecting to APAC locations: Malaysia (18ms), Indonesia (28ms), Thailand (20ms), Vietnam (22ms), India (38ms), Japan (52ms), Australia (48ms).

Must feel like: cloud infrastructure, global networking, premium SaaS, developer infrastructure, Nxeon branding.
Must NOT feel like: a gaming website, a generic geographic map/Google Maps, a stock illustration, a generic neon sci-fi dashboard.

BUILD WITH REAL CODE — SVG/HTML/CSS/React/CSS-or-SVG animation. Do NOT use the reference image as a background image or place it directly in the page. Recreate it.

Nxeon color tokens to use: background #050A16, secondary navy #081124, blue #1677FF, bright blue #3B82F6, purple #7C3AED, bright purple #8B5CF6, text #F8FAFC, muted text #94A3B8. No orange/yellow/red. Green only for tiny live/status dots if needed. Main network lighting transitions blue→purple.

Detailed spec (read the reference image directly for anything ambiguous below):
- Deep navy/black background, extremely subtle radial blue/purple ambient glow around Singapore, a barely-visible thin blue/navy perspective grid behind everything for depth (not distracting).
- APAC landmass rendered as a dotted/pixel-grid silhouette (dots, not solid polygons) — India, Southeast Asia, East Asia/Japan, Indonesia, Australia recognizable but not a literal detailed map. Dot brightness increases near important regions/routes.
- Singapore: powerful glowing central node, positioned center/lower-center — white/blue core, blue ring, purple outer ring, large soft radial glow, multiple concentric rings, slow subtle pulse (2-3s cycle, no flashing). This is the single most visually important element.
- Curved SVG paths (not straight lines) from Singapore to each of the 7 locations. Thin base stroke, blue/purple gradient, soft glow, brighter near Singapore fading outward. Small glowing node at each route's endpoint, gently pulsing, offset timing so they don't pulse in sync (3-5s cycle), all dimmer than the Singapore node.
- Animated particles traveling along each route from Singapore outward, 1-3 per route, varied speeds, SVG animation or CSS — this reads as live network traffic. Keep total DOM/element count light — no canvas particle systems, no Three.js/WebGL, no thousands of DOM nodes.
- Floating glass-style labels at each endpoint: dark translucent background, subtle blue border, slight blur, small radius, white text, latency number in bright blue, small country flag emoji. Singapore's own label is larger/more prominent with a stronger purple/blue border, attached to the central node.
- Visual hierarchy front-to-back: Singapore node > routes > dotted map > labels > ambient grid.
- Data-driven, not hardcoded JSX: a `locations` array (name, latency, x, y, maybe label-side) that generates nodes/routes/labels — make it easy to add/remove a location later.
- Component API: `<SingaporeNetworkMap showLabels={true} animated={true} />`, defaults matching the reference appearance exactly.
- Responsive: full graphic scales down on tablet; on mobile it remains a real standalone visual (not hidden), Singapore node must stay visible.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion (disable/simplify animation, keep the static composition).
- Performance: lightweight SVG + CSS, must stay smooth on normal laptops and mobile.

ITERATE FOR REAL: after your first build, render it standalone (a throwaway test page is fine, e.g. app/(marketing)/singapore-vps-hosting/page.tsx can temporarily render just `<SingaporeNetworkMap />` full-bleed on a plain dark page for screenshotting purposes — or a dedicated /dev-preview route if that's cleaner — your call, just make it screenshot-able), screenshot it with Playwright (require('playwright') resolves from /opt/nxeon/node_modules, set NODE_PATH=/opt/nxeon/node_modules, viewport 1536x1000+ to match the reference's wide aspect ratio), Read your screenshot AND the reference image side by side, and compare against this checklist the owner gave verbatim:
✓ Same overall visual concept ✓ Same Singapore-centered network ✓ Same APAC geography ✓ Same blue/purple color treatment ✓ Same glowing routes ✓ Same dotted map aesthetic ✓ Same floating latency labels ✓ Same central Singapore emphasis ✓ Actual animated network traffic ✓ Responsive behavior ✓ Reusable component

Do at least 3 rounds of build→screenshot→compare→adjust before considering this done — iterate on node positions, route curvature, map scale, label positioning, glow intensity, dot density, background grid, typography, animation speed as needed. Do not stop at the first acceptable version.

Setup: `git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-sgmap -b feature/singapore-network-map main` from /opt/nxeon. Symlink node_modules/.env from /opt/nxeon (`ln -sfn /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`, `ln -sf /opt/nxeon/.env .env`) — check `df -h /` has 5GB+ free first. Verify npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build clean. Remove .next from the worktree when done (leave node_modules symlink, don't delete the real target). Revert any throwaway preview-page wiring you added for screenshotting unless it's genuinely useful to keep — the owner did not ask for the map to be wired into any page yet, just built as a standalone reusable component; if you do leave a preview route in for convenience, make that explicit in your report. Commit clearly (Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>). Do not merge to main, do not touch the rejected /opt/nxeon-wt-sghero worktree.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE: a previous agent working on this same server caused a real (brief, auto-recovered) production outage by running `pkill -f "next start"` to clean up its own leftover dev/test process, which also matched production's real running service. Do NOT use broad pkill/pgrep patterns to manage your own dev/preview server processes — use specific PIDs you captured yourself when starting the process, or a fixed unusual port you can target precisely, and double-check what a kill command would match before running it.

Report back: screenshot paths from each comparison round, what changed each round and why, final screenshot, confirmation of build/tsc passing, and whether you left a preview route wired up.

## Summary

Built `SingaporeNetworkMap`, a standalone, reusable, data-driven React component, in a new worktree at `/opt/nxeon-wt-sgmap` (branch `feature/singapore-network-map`), without touching the rejected `nxeon-wt-sghero` worktree.

**File:** `/opt/nxeon-wt-sgmap/components/marketing/SingaporeNetworkMap.tsx` (339 lines, single commit `a0ab3e3`)

**Approach:** Pure SVG + CSS, no images/canvas/WebGL. The dotted APAC landmass (India, mainland SE Asia/China, Philippines, Sumatra/Java/Borneo belt, Japan, Australia, plus two decorative edge fragments) is drawn as hand-authored polygons used only as SVG `clipPath`s, filled via a tiny tiled dot `<pattern>`, with a radial-gradient `<mask>` brightening dots near Singapore and each destination node — so the "thousands of dots" visual costs only ~20 DOM nodes, not thousands. Routes are quadratic-bezier curves sharing one global horizontal linear gradient (blue near Singapore, purple toward the eastern destinations), with 2 CSS `offset-path` particles per route for live traffic, gently pulsing endpoint nodes, and a multi-ring glowing Singapore hub. Labels are HTML glass-pill overlays (backdrop-blur) positioned by percentage from the `LOCATIONS` data array, sized with `cqw`/`clamp()` via a `container-type: inline-size` wrapper.

**Iteration (4 rounds, screenshots in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/shots/`):**
1. `round1.png` — first pass; solid overall match but landmasses read as sparse disconnected blobs (Australia especially), routes lacked visible purple.
2. `round2.png` — enlarged/densified all landmass polygons, narrowed the route gradient range so Vietnam/Japan/Australia read clearly purple while the western routes stay blue (matches reference), boosted Singapore's glow. Investigated an apparent "missing Australia" via `debug_australia.png` — confirmed via cropped `crop_australia.png` it was rendering correctly, just faint at thumbnail scale.
3. `round3.png` — added two decorative edge landmass fragments to fill negative space like the reference, boosted dot pattern brightness/size for better readability at normal viewing scale.
4. Verified `motion_a.png`/`motion_b.png` (particles genuinely animate), `reduced_motion.png` (static, correct), and `mobile.png`/`mobile_crop.png` — found and fixed a real bug: right-side labels (Australia, Singapore) got sliced off by the component's own `overflow: hidden` on narrow widths. Fixed with a `@container` breakpoint (≤430px) that collapses labels to flag-only badges. Re-verified with `mobile_crop2.png` (no overflow) and `round4_final.png` (desktop unaffected).
